proof:
Only the case $F_-,F_+>0$ requires a bound. There $H(w_-),H(w_+)>0$, and concavity gives $H(w_0)\ge(H(w_-)+H(w_+))/2>0$. Write $R_i=(g_iH(w_i))^{1/(d-m)}$. For $r>0$ the map $(U,h)\mapsto(U^rh)^{1/(r+1)}$ is increasing in its coordinates and concave, as follows by minimizing $(raU+a^{-r}h)/(r+1)$ over $a>0$. Its interior critical point gives the equality, and zero values follow by limits. Apply monotonicity and concavity with $U_i=g_i^{1/r}$ and $h_i=H(w_i)$ to get $R_0\ge(R_-+R_+)/2$. For $r=0$ one has $d-m=1$, and the maximum assumption gives $g_0H(w_0)\ge(g_-H(w_-)+g_+H(w_+))/2$. This proves the same bound.

If $m>0$, put $p=d/m>1$. Then $F_i^{-1/m}=L(w_i)^p/R_i^{p-1}$. The map $(L,R)\mapsto R(L/R)^p$ is convex by Jensen with weights proportional to the respective $R$ values; it increases in $L$ and decreases in $R$. Use convexity of $L$, the inequality for $R_0$, and convexity of this map to bound $F_0^{-1/m}$ above by the mean of the two endpoint values. If $m=0$, then $F_i=(R_i/L(w_i))^d$ and
$$
\frac{R_0}{L(w_0)}\ge\frac{R_-+R_+}{L(w_-)+L(w_+)}
\ge\min\left(\frac{R_-}{L(w_-)},\frac{R_+}{L(w_+)}\right).
$$
With a vanishing endpoint the desired inequality just states nonnegativity. Finally on the convex region $H>0$ the same monotonicity and concavity proof makes $R=(gH)^{1/(d-m)}$ concave, using arbitrary convex weights, and the same perspective argument makes the inverse power convex.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and $0\le m\le d-1$. At physical points $w_-,w_+,w_0=(w_-+w_+)/2$ let $g_-,g_+,g_0>0$ be finite. For $r=d-1-m>0$ assume $g_0^{1/r}\ge(g_-^{1/r}+g_+^{1/r})/2$, and for $r=0$ assume $g_0\ge\max(g_-,g_+)$. Let $H$ be one finite concave function and $L$ one finite positive convex function on a convex domain containing the three points. Put $F_i=g_i(H(w_i))_+/L(w_i)^d$. If $m>0$ then
$$
F_0\ge\left[\frac{F_-^{-1/m}+F_+^{-1/m}}2\right]^{-m},
$$
with the right side defined as zero if either endpoint vanishes. For $m=0$ one has $F_0\ge\min(F_-,F_+)$. On a face interior of dimension $m>0$ with the positive density representative whose $1/r$ power is concave for $r>0$, or whose density is constant for $r=0$, $(gH/L^d)^{-1/m}$ is convex on the relative-interior region $H>0$.
title: Shared concave numerator and convex denominator give midpoint capacities
